studies.title: Working on an algorithm-controlled platform as a content creator: what explains unequal earnings on YouTube?
studies.scope: YouTube channels from Germany, Austria and Switzerland
studies.estimation_note: Paper's abstract reports an earnings-inequality Gini of 0.89; exact underlying earnings methodology and sample sizes must be checked against full paper before interpreting it as actual payouts.
findings: Earnings are strongly skewed in the study's channel dataset.
The authors report a Gini coefficient of 0.89 for the earnings measure they analyze.
limitations: Geography is limited to Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
Methods and whether money is observed or modeled were not established by reading the full PDF.
No general median or mean for all YouTube creators can be inferred.
Channel sample recruitment details not established from this abstract.

studies.title: How do users contribute to YouTube channels’ revenue? An empirical analysis of Korean beauty channels
studies.scope: 50 Korean beauty YouTube channels analyzed using channel Analytics and panel fixed-effects regressions
studies.estimation_note: Channel Analytics panel regressions analyze associations between user watch-time measures and monthly channel revenue.
findings: Returning-viewer watch time was the strongest revenue-associated measure examined.
New-viewer and subscriber watch time were positively associated with revenue; likes were not statistically significant in this analysis.
limitations: Small selected channel sample in one country and niche.
Fixed-effects regression associations are not randomized causal effects.
No country-generalized beauty niche RPM or newcomer earnings provided.
The public abstract does not establish whole-platform selection or profit after production costs.

studies.title: Creator strategies in the platform economy: How frequency, consistency, and content type affect YouTube engagement, attention, and revenue
studies.scope: 47 Korea-based YouTube beauty channels, examining frequency, consistency and video format
studies.estimation_note: Paper's abstract reports statistically significant prediction/association with viewer engagement, return measures and revenue.
findings: Upload frequency was statistically associated with reported engagement and revenue.
Regular publishing was associated with audience loyalty.
A higher concentration of Shorts was associated with lower sustained viewing time in the studied channels.
limitations: Channel sample is 47, not all Korean channels or all genres.
Cross-sectional and longitudinal confounding may remain; findings do not prove a causal posting schedule.
No universal optimal weekly upload frequency or creator-income prediction follows.
Full data/method tables are not analyzed here.

studies.title: Who Reaps All the Superchats? A Large-Scale Analysis of Income Inequality in Virtual YouTuber Livestreaming
studies.scope: 1,923 VTubers and over one million hours of publicly accessible YouTube live-stream records
studies.estimation_note: Public live-event records and Super Chat signals, not a census of total VTuber income.
findings: Authors analyze the concentration and inequality of monetized live viewer contributions among sampled virtual performers.
limitations: Public live chat/stream records are not total channel income, after-fee receipts or profit.
Sampling details and economic statistics beyond the abstract need full-text assessment.
VTuber experiences cannot be generalized to all live creators or video formats.

rules: A reported Gini coefficient is not an ordinary creator's pay and cannot define a median or mean without distribution data.
A fixed-effects association is not by itself an experimentally identified causal result.
Comparisons between niches require like-for-like source populations and periods.
Super Chat transaction records are not complete publisher profits.
Full-text sample construction, data provenance and author-disclosed methods remain an explicit separate task.
Do not represent estimated earnings as personally verified YouTube Studio payments.
